episodes.213718: Monsoon moisture across eastern and southern New Mexico combined with daytime heating resulted in diurnal thunderstorm activity first across the higher terrain midday before moving into nearby lower elevations during the afternoon and evening hours on July 10th and 11th. Thunderstorms resulted in flash flooding and debris flow on and downstream of the burn scars surrounding Ruidoso both afternoons, and severe wind gusts near Ragland in Quay County the evening of July 10th and at two mesonet stations on White Sands Missile Range the evening of July 11th. Thunderstorms slowly diminished just before midnight both days.
episodes.213950: Moisture was high for mid July across the combined Panhandles with precipitable water values in the 90th percentile.  This would result in efficient rainfall occurring from any storm that developed during the afternoon and evening hours of July 12th. A weak upper level disturbance moved across the region, and coupled with heating and unstable atmosphere, was able to produce some showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon. Outflow boundaries also contributed to additional storm development, including one that formed across the city of Amarillo and persisted for a long time. This storm produced efficient heavy rainfall that resulted in significant flooding across downtown and the southern sections of the city. Additionally, damaging winds and even a landspout occurred during these storms.
episodes.214020: A line of thunderstorms developed across Lake Superior during the early afternoon hours on Sunday (7/12) and tracked south through the lakeshore counties of northeast Wisconsin during the mid-afternoon.  The strongest storms produced damaging winds across Door County.
episodes.214021: A line of thunderstorms produced strong winds over Lake Michigan and the bay of Green Bay during the afternoon hours on Sunday (7/12).
episodes.214059: Strong thunderstorms moved through Petroleum and southern Phillips Counties, a few of which became severe.
episodes.214117: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of northeastern Oklahoma during the evening of the 11th, near a stationary front that stretched across the region, as an upper level disturbance translated into the area. The strongest storms produced damaging wind gusts and large hail to half dollar size.
episodes.214232: On the afternoon of the 12th, numerous thunderstorm outflow boundaries collided across the South Plains of West Texas. A very unstable atmosphere allowed scattered thunderstorms to develop. Although most of these storms were non-severe, a few severe wind gusts did occur across Lubbock County. A wet microburst occurred south of Idalou (Lubbock County) which caused roof damage to a barn and mobile homes. One outflow boundary over Lubbock County was slow moving which generated slow moving thunderstorms. Localized areas of heavy rainfall occurred over northwestern portions of the city of Lubbock and the city of Slaton where multiple vehicles became stalled in flood waters.
episodes.214287: A frontal boundary sagged into the Midlands of SC where it then stalled with a sharp shortwave moving into the region. Along and south of the boundary robust instability developed with weak effective shear from the shortwave. Profiles became conducive for damaging winds. Scattered tree damage was reported across the Midlands.
episodes.214302: Monsoon storms formed on the afternoon of July 12th producing damaging winds and heavy rain that led to flash flooding.
episodes.214582: Thunderstorms produced isolated wind damage near Jersey Village.
episodes.214845: Typical summer weather prevailed with scattered afternoon and evening storms, some of which were severe. Unfortunately, two fatalities occurred in Tallahassee on July 10th when a large tree fell on a moving vehicle.
episodes.214945: Typical summer weather prevailed with scattered afternoon and evening storms, some of which were severe.
episodes.214947: Typical summer weather prevailed with scattered afternoon and evening storms, some of which were severe.
episodes.215057: A squall line of storms downed trees and powerlines in Florence County, SC.
episodes.215271: Despite drier air aloft affecting portions of the area thanks to the Saharan Air Layer, enough moisture and instability was in place for scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms to develop across northeast FL. Southwest flow mainly focus isolated strong to severe convection over the eastern half of the region. Presence of dry air aloft likely played into stronger downbursts and areas of wind damage across northeast FL.
episodes.215465: A large cluster of thunderstorms developed inland across the South Carolina Midlands in the early afternoon hours. These storms eventually moved across the South Carolina Lowcountry and into the Atlantic coastal waters, producing strong wind gusts into the early evening hours. A few additional storms developed along the southeast Georgia coast later in the evening and produced strong wind gusts further to the south.
episodes.215515: A slow moving cold front gradually pushed its way south and eastwards across Eastern North Carolina eventually stalling across the Pamlico Sound during the overnight hours of July eleventh. Out ahead and along this front clusters of thunderstorms developed impacting the waters of Eastern North Carolina. With ample instability in place a few of these storms became strong to severe in nature bringing damaging wind gusts to portions of the Pamlico Rover during the evening hours of July eleventh.
episodes.215564: Clusters of thunderstorms developed along the southeast Georgia and southeast South Carolina coast in the afternoon hours. These storms produced strong wind gusts along the coast and across portions of the adjacent Atlantic coastal waters in the afternoon and early evening.
episodes.215569: Scattered thunderstorms developed across portions of southeast South Carolina in the afternoon hours. A few of these storms became strong enough to produce damaging wind gusts into the early evening.
episodes.215571: Scattered thunderstorms developed across portions of southeast Georgia in the afternoon hours. A few of these storms became strong enough to produce some minor wind damage into the early evening.
episodes.215632: Slow moving frontal system provided the impetus for a long duration heavy rainfall threat that yielded significant flash flooding in Cocke County and Greene County. Additionally, a severe downburst occurred late in day in Jefferson County.
episodes.215985: A convective cluster impacted portions of northern and central Oklahoma on the early morning of the 12th. This activity produced strong to locally severe wind gusts.
episodes.216183: Behind a back door cold front, widespread showers and thunderstorms developed from the late afternoon through the early overnight hours. Numerous reports of flash flooding were reported, along with several damaging wind reports.
episodes.216393: A slow moving upper low approached from the northwest on the 12th, pushing a frontal boundary through the area late in the day and sparking off yet another day of widespread showers and thunderstorms across the southern Appalachian region. This resulted in some scattered reports of flash flooding in East Tennessee.
episodes.216517: Increasing moisture and instability developed isolated thunderstorms across North-Central MT during the afternoon. Strong synoptic winds and hot and dry surface conditions brought a favorable environment for gusty dry downbursts.
episodes.216543: A stationary frontal boundary took up residency over the Central Appalachians beginning on July 10th, supplying ample moisture for multiple days of heavy rain over West Virginia. Showers and thunderstorms, mainly observed during peak heating hours, promoted instances of flash flooding from July 11th to July 12th over the southern half of the state. Impassable roadways due to high water were the main impacts from this stretch of heavy rain, with water receding by the evening each day once convective activity came to an end.
episodes.216546: Back to back days of flash flooding occurred in Buchanan County on July 11th and 12th as a result of a nearby frontal boundary. The front parked itself over the Central Appalachians during this time, providing the necessary components of moisture and instability to stir up daily showers and storms in the region. Activity in southwest Virginia was observed during the mornings on both of these days, and resulted in brief road closures due to high water. The front gained momentum once again and departed offshore heading into the middle of July, which limited the flooding threat and brought the return of dry weather for a few days in southwest Virginia.
episodes.216589: Onshore westerly sea breeze flow and a shortwave aloft approaching the SE U.S. combined to produce early afternoon convection that produced a strong marine wind gust near Cedar Key.
episodes.216665: During mid-July, a slow-moving easterly wave brought sufficient moisture and lift to trigger showers and thunderstorms across portions of Central and North Texas. Flash flooding occurred in multiple areas due to the influx of tropical moisture, weak flow aloft, and slow storm movement.
episodes.216689: Multiple minor disturbances around a high pressure over the Upper Midwest initiated thunderstorms which crossed Lake Superior from the northwest and caused severe weather for various UP locations (including Isle Royale National Park).
episodes.216727: Strong thunderstorms moved across the marine area and produced gusty winds.
episodes.216760: A weak frontal boundary approached the northern Gulf Coast on July 12th while an upper-level trough moved into the southeastern United States. Abundant moisture supported numerous showers and thunderstorms over the coastal waters, particularly during the afternoon hours. A few of those thunderstorms produced locally strong wind gusts over local coastal waters.
episodes.216791: Multiple minor disturbances moving around an upper level ridge of high pressure over the Upper Midwest initiated thunderstorms which crossed Lake Superior from the northwest.
episodes.216827: Thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts along the Brevard and Treasure Coasts.
episodes.216897: Upper level troughing remained over southwest Louisiana during multiple days in mid July. This allowed scattered storms to develop each day with some producing heavy rain.
episodes.217041: Strong heating a high humidity allowed for scattered afternoon thunderstorm development with locally heavy rainfall.
episodes.217105: From July 11th into the 12th, a slow-moving mid-level trough and surface front was draped across the Ohio and Tennessee Valleys, providing the conditions for a period of unsettled weather. During the afternoon hours on July 11th, daytime heating allowed temperatures to rise into the mid-to-upper 80s, with dew point temperatures in the low-to-mid 70s, creating a typical summertime unstable environment with between 1500 and 2500 J/kg of mixed-layer CAPE. While the mid- and upper-level disturbance over the region was not particularly amplified, it did allow a band of 30 knot mid-level winds to set up over south central Kentucky, which supported effective bulk shear values of 30-35 knots. Scattered multicell thunderstorms produced a few instances of wind damage in Warren and Barren County, with storms gradually weakening during the late evening hours on the 11th. However, overnight from the 11th into the 12th, as a cutoff low pivoted slowly across the area, slow-moving showers and thunderstorms continued to produce areas of flash flooding across central and southern Kentucky. Decreasing, but sufficient instability and precipitable water values near or over 2 inches resulted in efficient rainfall producing showers and storms which finally began to dissipate during the evening hours on July 12th.
episodes.217149: Scattered thunderstorms developed over the Carolina Piedmont during the afternoon. One of the storms moved into Union County, NC from South Carolina and produced brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.217150: Isolated thunderstorms developed over northeast Georgia during the late afternoon. One of the storms produced a small area of damaging wind gusts in Habersham County.

episodes.217262: An upper level disturbance arrived and lingered over South Florida in early to mid June which produced a period of unsettled weather.

The severe thunderstorm winds caused damage across the Tucson Metro an in Lavender Farms . Additionally, the heavy rainfall caused running washes that led to 3 water rescues in the Tucson Metro and impassable roadways.

The collision of two outflow boundaries right over Amarillo created additional thunderstorms that produced efficient rainfall of likely two to three inch per hour rainfall rates. These storms did not move out of the area quickly and heavy rainfall resulted in widespread flash flooding, especially across portions of the southwest side of the city. Fast moving flood waters occurred across many streets and parking lots, some of which were anywhere from six to eight inches deep or even up to 12 inches deep. There were multiple to numerous impassable roads with swift flowing water across them and water up to the wheel wells of many cars and SUVs. Several vehicles were stalled and flooded on the roads. Water flooded into some structures. This included Amarillo Square Apartments, which had two feet of water inside ground floor apartment units. In addition, dumpsters were being moved by these fast moving flood waters in some residential areas.
